fact: The ECA Director General told Shega the Authority had received about 10 requests to transfer data abroad and had approved them as a temporary measure, and officials previewed a forthcoming registration portal for data controllers and processors at a workshop co-hosted with Huawei; the article records no sanction or published count of decisions, noting that as of March 2025 no ECA enforcement actions or guidelines had been publicized.

Techhive Advisory says Ethiopia's Personal Data Protection Proclamation was published in the Federal Negarit Gazette on 24 July 2024, bringing it into effect, and that Articles 18-21 make international transfers depend on an Authority adequacy decision, explicit consent of the data subject, necessity, or public registry purposes, with sensitive data transfers needing the Authority's prior authorisation.

The law firm Haymanot & Advocates says Directive SBB/94/2025 makes transfers abroad of non-customer data by banks conditional on National Bank of Ethiopia prior written approval, disclosure of destinations, adequate protection in the receiving jurisdiction and service level agreements.

Digital Policy Alert records that Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024, adopted by Parliament on 4 April 2024, entered into force on 24 July 2024 and requires data controllers and processors to store locally collected personal data on servers in Ethiopia.

Digital Policy Alert states that the Personal Data Protection Proclamation, implemented in July 2024, requires controllers and processors to store personal data collected locally on a server or data centre within Ethiopia.

Digital Policy Alert states that in August 2021 the Ethiopian Communications Authority adopted a consumer rights directive requiring telecom providers to process consumer personal data only on servers or data centres in Ethiopia.

Birr Metrics reports that Ethiopia's Personal Data Protection Proclamation of 2024 mandates that data collected domestically be stored within the country, with cross-border transfers permitted only under strict conditions.
Xalam Analytics says the Personal Data Protection Proclamation of 2024 requires companies to host Ethiopian citizen data within the country.

The law firm Haymanot & Advocates says National Bank of Ethiopia Directive No. SBB/94/2025 requires all banks, foreign subsidiaries and branches included, to store and process customer and core banking data, primary and backup, within Ethiopia.

The African Union Commission's status list dated 2 February 2026 shows Ethiopia with no date of signature, no date of ratification or accession and no date of deposit for the Malabo Convention (21 of 55 states signed, 20 ratified).
